title: The Oath of the Sundered Sea
premise: Gideon Thackeray, a mercenary who once swore an oath to a god that has since gone silent, hides in plain sight as the ledger-keeper of the Vesperline Guild, which traffics in impossible things: bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When a mute child arrives at the guild's door speaking a language older than any living kingdom, Gideon realizes the child is a living key to the Sundered Sea—the drowned country Gideon's god died defending—and that the guild's masters intend to sell the key to the empire that did the drowning. Hunted by her own guild and haunted by the god's last unanswered prayer, Gideon gathers a ragtag found family of debtors, smugglers, and one very old liar, and sets out to find the door out of a country that no longer exists. In the end, Gideon must choose between renewing her oath and telling the truth that would free the child—and the god's silence breaks only when she chooses love over duty, opening the door at the cost of the guild, the ledgers, and the life she built to stay invisible.
about_author: Ines Eriksen is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the logbooks of ships that never came home, a habit that seeps into everything she writes. She lives on a cold northern coast, where she writes fantasy about oaths, drowned places, and the people who keep the books.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unspent Words
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A night of routine ledger-keeping at the Vesperline Guild establishes her careful, invisible life and the silent god she still prays to out of habit. The emotional beat is quiet dread: she has kept her oaths for eleven years and received nothing back, and she is beginning to wonder if faith without answer is just stubbornness wearing a nicer coat.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A mute girl arrives soaked in seawater that smells of a country Gideon thought was legend, speaking in a tongue that makes the guild's oldest artifacts hum. Gideon hides her before the guild's enforcers find her. The beat is reluctant tenderness—the first crack in Gideon's armor of neutrality, as the child's language is the last prayer Gideon ever spoke to her god.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys and Sells
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with a flashback in the guildmaster's voice. Gideon discovers a purchase order in the ledgers: the empire has contracted the Vesperline to deliver 'a living key, female, under twelve years.' She understands the child is merchandise. The beat is betrayal—Gideon realizes her invisibility made her complicit, and that ledgers record sins as neatly as they record debts.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Ryn Okonjo's POV, a smuggler who owes the guild nine impossible favors. Gideon calls in a favor to move the child out of the city, and Ryn grudgingly agrees, recognizing in Gideon a fellow survivor of a broken oath. The beat is wary alliance—two people who trust no one deciding, provisionally, to trust each other.

chapters.title: The Old Liar of Lantern Wharf
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Ryn POVs. They seek out Sable Vane, an ancient information-broker who once sailed the Sundered Sea and who owes Gideon's dead god a debt of his own. Sable confirms the child is the last native speaker—and the only living map to the door. The beat is grief disguised as wit: Sable laughs through the whole interview, and only his hands shake.

chapters.title: Hunted by the Book
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The guild turns Gideon's own ledgers against her, reconstructing her movements from her meticulous records; enforcers corner the trio at Lantern Wharf. Ryn takes a blade meant for the child, and they barely escape by sea. The beat is guilt sharpened into resolve—Gideon's precision, her one virtue, has become the noose, and she burns her own ledger to break the trail.

chapters.title: Where the Map Is a Mouth
chapters.summary: The child's POV, rendered in close, wordless perception. Sailing toward the drowned coast, the child begins to speak—not words Gideon understands, but songs that make the sea rise in shapes. Gideon realizes the door out of the Sundered Sea doesn't open; it answers. The beat is wonder and fear: the child is not a key to be used but a voice to be heard, and Gideon's plan has treated her as cargo.

chapters.title: The Empire's Patience
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. The empire's envoy arrives, and Corvane, who once loved Gideon as a daughter, is given an ultimatum: deliver the traitor and the key, or the guild burns. Corvane chooses the guild. The beat is tragic duty—Corvane is not a monster but a mirror, showing Gideon exactly what she becomes if she keeps choosing the institution over the person.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. At the drowned coast, the guild, the empire, and Gideon's ragged family converge on the place where the Sundered Sea used to be. Gideon must speak the god's last prayer—the one she never finished—to open the door, and the guildmaster offers her everything she lost if she'll hand over the child. The beat is the central choice: Gideon kneels, not to her god or her guild, but to the child, and tells the whole truth of her silence. The door opens on truth, not oath, and the god's voice returns—not to command, but to say goodbye.

chapters.title: Ledgers Kept in Salt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, resolution. The guild is shattered, the empire's claim broken by a door that closed behind the child's people, and Gideon stays on the coast with Ryn, Sable, and a scarred, quieter life. She keeps a new ledger—not of debts, but of names. The beat is earned peace: love against duty was never a war to win, only a choice to keep making, and for the first time, Gideon's prayers are answered with silence that feels like company rather than absence.
